title: XAGR: Explainable-Aligned Gradient Regularisation for Deepfake Image Detection
verified_identity: Preet Kaur and Anuj Kumar Gupta; 16-page SSRN preprint posted 2026-06-13; the official SSRN page explicitly labels it as not peer-reviewed.
scope_reviewed: Visually reviewed the 16-page official SSRN PDF: body pages 1-14 (abstract/introduction, related work, framework/objective, data split, results/figures, conclusion and declarations). PDF bibliography positions [1]-[31] on pages 14-16 were crosschecked against the already-completed T161 screen in T231; no second thematic screen or new reference-position count is claimed. This is a targeted evidence review, not a claim of a separate independent replication.
methods_and_sample: Training-time XAGR adds a regularization term to classification cross-entropy to align normalized Saliency and Grad-CAM maps. Important formula discrepancy: Eq. (2) and the printed algorithm read Mean(|S_norm(x)| - |G_norm(x)|), with no outer absolute value around the map difference; since min-max-normalized maps are nonnegative, this typeset expression is a signed mean difference, not a pixelwise absolute-distance objective. Figure 2 appears to depict an absolute map difference, so the intended training objective is ambiguous; no code was verified. The later evaluation equations (4)-(6) separately define absolute per-pixel map discrepancy. Evaluation uses Celeb-DF v2 only: 24,000 selected frames (12,000 real/12,000 fake), split 16,800/3,600/3,600, across five CNNs. The paper does not establish a video-disjoint split. For EfficientNet-B0, accuracy changes .83611 to .84028, F1 decreases .83682 to .82684, and AUC changes .9235 to .9250; gains are not uniform across the tested architectures.
observed_reliability_evidence: Evaluation equations (4)-(6), not the ambiguous Eq. (2) training objective, report mean absolute per-pixel discrepancy between the normalized Saliency and Grad-CAM maps. For EfficientNet-B0 it falls from 0.132 to 0.055 (58.31%). This supports greater agreement between these two attribution maps under the paper's evaluation calculation. It does not show that either map is correct.
limitations_and_construct_boundary: Eq. (2)/algorithm and Figure 2 are inconsistent about whether the training alignment loss takes an absolute difference; absent verified code, the trained objective cannot be confidently characterized as pixelwise MAE. Evaluation MAE is a cross-explainer agreement measure, not an independent localization/forensic-ground-truth test. The reviewed body reports no independent tampered-region/artifact ground truth, causal/counterfactual evaluation, parameter-randomization sanity check, deletion/insertion test, explanation annotator/human rating, inter-rater agreement, or user-reliance study. One dataset is used; cross-dataset validation is future work. Split independence at the source-video level is not established. The SSRN record labels the paper as not peer reviewed.
screening_conclusion: Retain as a directly relevant deepfake-image explanation-consistency study with targeted official full-text evidence. Its reported reliability signal is evaluation-time inter-explainer map agreement only; its training objective is ambiguous as printed. Do not describe it as validating explanation truth, causal faithfulness, forensic evidence grounding, robustness, or calibrated human reliance.
